title: ID0422203-DC/Si-D/MY-[MP / ND 170000121] charging failure with remotestart
description:
Reported behavior/issue: We have been encountering issues where generally remotestart accepted but
charging session was not initiated. Need this to be troubleshot and identified
if this is a software or hardware issues.
Resolution
: In
crease the ConnectionTimeOut, Authorize first and plug in later. Update charger to latest FW.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0422203-DC/Si-D/MY-[MP / ND 170000121] Intermittent Issues CRM:02679000212
additional_info.body:
Hello Syabil,
Upon checking the logs, I see there are 3 reasons for charging session failure, with RemoteStart.
It happens only when there is a parallel charging (Both outlets being used).
There was >30 sec delay between RemoteStartTransaction command and plugging EV or vice-versa.
On Outlet 1 there was Insulation monitoring device error as well (Can be beucase of parallel charging or timeout).
I have noticed that the charger is running on very old FW version v4.0.11, however the latest release is v7.0.5.
To perform the detailed, analysis, I would recommend updating the charger to the latest version and test the RemoteStart functionality again.
The update path to 7.0.5 will, 4.0.11 > 5.0.23 > 6.1.3 > 7.0.5, i.e. there will be 3 updates.
To update the charger remotely, it will require ~ 6GB of data, may you please confirm if the SIM card inside the charger has adequate data plan to update the charger and troubleshoot further.
Additionally, we would like to know the list of EV's that you are experiencing issue with.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0422203-DC/Si-D/MY-[MP / ND 170000121] Intermittent Issues CRM:02679000212
additional_info.body:
Hello All,
I will wait for your confirmation before staring any FW update on this charger due to data limit.
To answer your question about the timeout, there are two communication process that works in parallel while EV Charging.
EVSE-EV
: CCS communication, it start from SLAC process, immediately after the cable is plugged in, and reaches to “
Authorization
” or “
ContractAuthentication
” state, where EVSE is awaiting an Authentication from user/OCPP. It can be a local Authorization or remote.
EVSE-CS
(Central System): OCPP, All messages related to charger status, User Authentication, Start/Stop Transaction Metervalues etc.
CCS and OCPP messages have their independent timeouts, the most common is the one which is at the “
Authorization
” stage.
Charger cannot Reject the
RemoteStartTransaction
, simply because the EV-EVSE communication is timed out in absence of user authentication, which can be a local or remote.
As EVSE-EV and EVSE-CS communication are separate.
I hope the above answer helps. Let me know if you need further clarification.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Reetesh Sharma

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0422203-DC/Si-D/MY-[MP / ND 170000121] Intermittent Issues CRM:02679000212
additional_info.body:
Hello Bryan,
Please find my answers here:
1. Does Authorize message help on this method? some charger we meet it will send Authorize massage after we send RemoteStart.
[RS]: No, sending Authorize.req after RemoteStartTransaction is optional, it will not make any difference in this scenario.
2. Besides to check the time from Status Notification "Preparing".is there a way to know that, the EVSE-EV communication already timeout?
[RS]: No, the charger will change status notification only when the communication has failed and the CP state is changed to “F”
3. Can the  EVSE-EV communication timeout be configurable?
[RS]: No, as this is related to DIN/ISO communication protocol performance timing messages and not related to OCPP.
4. What is the definition of the "ConnectionTimeOutCountdown" key from GetConfiguration?
[RS]: This key additional parameter for displaying when the timeout will be reached.
You can try to follow these steps to mitigate the Authorization delay.
Set the ConnectionTimeOut key to 90
Ask user to Authorize RemoteStart first and then plug in the EV within 90 Sec.
Hope this helps, Let me know if you need additional information, looking forward to received your feedback.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Reetesh Sharma

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0422203-DC/Si-D/MY-[MP / ND 170000121] Intermittent Issues CRM:02679000212
additional_info.body:
Hello Reetesh Sharma,
1. Set the ConnectionTimeOut key to 90
[Bryan]: We had tried to set it to 0 and 86400, but still the same. Can you help to test this configuration key on your lab unit to see whether it can mitigate the problem?
[RS]: We have tested and verified this configuration change previously in different
version
with different CPO's and it works. Please try setting it between 90 to 120.
[Bryan]: The reason we set 0 or 86400, is because we don't want the connector status going back to "Available" from "Preparing" / "Finishing" while it is still connected, we need the connector status to follow the actual status to indicate it is "Connected" / "Disconnected" with EV.
2. Ask user to Authorize RemoteStart first and then plug in the EV within 90 Sec.

Hello Bryan,
Please see my response as:
1. Set the ConnectionTimeOut key to 90
[Bryan]: We had tried to set it to 0 and 86400, but still the same. Can you help to test this configuration key on your lab unit to see whether it can mitigate the problem?
[RS]: We have tested and verified this configuration change previously in different
version

[RS]: This configuration key is of most importance, when use Authorize first and plug in EV later. Not When the EV is plugged in first and Authorized later.
